name: Edward VII
role: King of the United Kingdom and the British Dominions, Emperor of India (1901-1910)
summary: A constitutional monarch whose record is mostly ministers' policy, with limited political writing of his own. His recorded views include opposition to Irish Home Rule, to women's suffrage and to protectionism, sympathy for trade unions and housing reform, and strong support for the navy and army reform. He sought to keep the House of Lords largely intact during the 1909-10 crisis.

notes: Born 1841, king 1901-1910. Lee's biography is an official, sympathetic work; where it characterises his views rather than quoting them, answers are held at low or medium. Most of his reign's policy was ministers' decisions and is not counted as his. Not accessed: Magnus's biography (not freely available), Hansard text of the 1884 speech (not found online). Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by evidence. The Gutenberg collection of his own speeches as Prince of Wales (1863-1888) is read by theme (housing, slavery, temperance, Ireland, free trade, the working classes) and cited; most of its pages are the editor's narrative of charity dinners, exhibitions and foundation stones, which state no position, and only the 1884 Lords housing speech and the Anti-Slavery chair speech are cited. His Irish toasts are explicitly non-political. The Wikipedia Royal Commission page is no longer cited alone.
